data.hook: Ever pushed through exhaustion for that extra edge, only to wonder if it's worth it? A fresh analysis of half a million people reveals a precise nightly sweet spot that guards against faster aging and early death.
data.name: New Study Pinpoints Ideal Sleep Range for Health and Longevity
data.summary: Researchers using UK Biobank data on about 500,000 adults found 6.4 to 7.8 hours of sleep per night optimal, with too little under six hours or too much beyond that linked to quicker biological aging in organs and higher mortality risk. The U-shaped pattern appears in a Nature-published study, showing both extremes raise disease chances. Online discussions highlight personal stories—like sleep-deprived productivity that fades after days—and pushback against ideas that less rest signals genius, underscoring the clash between hustle culture and science favoring steady, moderate sleep.

data.summary: Daylight saving time ended Sunday, November 1, 2026, across most of the U.S., turning back clocks at 2 a.m. and disrupting internal rhythms despite the extra hour. Many report crashing early—around 5:30 or 6 p.m.—or sleeping until afternoon, as earlier darkness triggers drowsiness before the body fully adjusts. Experts explain that reduced evening light plays a key role, with effects lingering days into November's shorter days; people are sharing tips and jokes about their low-energy slump.
